summary: The End Polluter Welfare Act of 2025 eliminates fossil fuel subsidies by repealing royalty relief and increasing royalty rates on federal leases, terminating numerous tax expenditures and deductions for oil gas and coal companies, prohibiting federal funding and loan guarantees for fossil fuel projects, and repealing recent laws that expanded such support.

scores.thoughts: The bill rescinds unobligated funds for the Office of Fossil Energy, prohibits use of appropriated funds for fossil fuel projects across multiple agencies and international institutions, eliminates loan guarantees and direct assistance tied to fossil fuels, and terminates various subsidy programs. These provisions directly reduce federal outlays and spending authority related to fossil fuels.

Title II terminates numerous tax expenditures, deductions, credits, and preferential treatments for fossil fuel companies (e.g., enhanced oil recovery credit, percentage depletion, LIFO inventory, intangible drilling costs). It also increases excise taxes (oil spill liability, Black Lung) and imposes new taxes (Gulf of Mexico severance tax). This raises effective tax burdens on fossil fuel corporations.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare coverage, markets, or public programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill contains no provisions that alter military or defense spending levels or priorities.

By systematically eliminating fossil fuel subsidies, royalty relief, tax preferences, and project financing, the bill reduces support for fossil fuel production and use. It also increases liability for oil spills and restricts international financing for fossil projects, directly advancing environmental protection goals.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, school choice, or federal education policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions that alter tariffs, trade agreements, or general trade policy; restrictions on export financing are narrowly environmental.
By rescinding spending, terminating subsidies, and raising revenues through higher royalties and new taxes, the bill reduces federal deficits and prioritizes fiscal restraint over new borrowing.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.

Sections 107 and 114 restrict or rescind U.S. contributions and financing through international financial institutions, development banks, and export agencies when used for fossil fuel projects, effectively curtailing certain forms of international spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill contains no provisions related to worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.
